messages:
IncidentBot: [P1] Streaming websocket errors for enterprise tenant 'Novus' on VPC gateway - surge of 502/WS_CLOSE (start 2218887700) :rotating_light:
Amanda L: paging oncall now, tagging oncall rota. initial symptom: customer reports app-side streaming disconnects, retries ballooning.
Amanda L: suspected correlation with yesterday's gateway canary (v1.14.3) rollout to dedicated/vpc route groups.
IncidentBot: Pager sent to Jess (oncall).
Jess (oncall): on it. grabbing logs from ingress and gw pools. any customer-facing outage? Sasha S (SE) - are they seeing errors from Novus app?
Sasha S (SE): Novus reported intermittent WS disconnects starting ~13:03 UTC, likely causing replay/retry loops. They show ~15-30s windows of successful streams then immediate close. They've paused client exponential backoff to reduce load while we triage.
Murat K: pulling gw metrics now. seeing a sharp uptick in `ws_conn_close` and `backend_502_rate` for vpc-route-group-novus. also seeing `backend_pong_latency_ms` spike.
Murat K: suspecting upstream idle/ping mismatch + a retries storm from Novus leading to connection churn.
Jess (oncall): good hypothesis. mitigation options: 1) route Novus traffic to their dedicated reserved pool (cold fallback) 2) short-circuit retries at gateway (reject instead of proxy) 3) bump ws keepalive/pong timeout on their route 4) rollback canary for gateway patch. Thoughts?
Sasha S (SE): Novus prefers minimal downtime. Option 1 (dedicated pool) is viable — they have reserved capacity. switching should be quick if we update routing policy, but need to coordinate and inform Novus. Option 3 is least disruptive, we can increase `pong_timeout_ms` and set `max_retries_per_conn` to 3.
Murat K: running a quick config change on staging showed reduced disconnects when `pong_timeout_ms` increased from 2000 -> 8000 and `max_retries_per_conn` limited. I'll prepare the config patch.
Jess (oncall): do it on prod canary first targeted to Novus route. Murat, please push patch and DeployBot do a scoped deploy. We need logs to confirm reduction before full rollout.
DeployBot: Received deploy request: gateway-config/2026-03-15/novus-ws-mitigation. Rolling to canary (route=novus) now.
Murat K: applying patch snippet:
```
route "novus" {
  pong_timeout_ms = 8000
  max_retries_per_conn = 3
  upstream_pool = "reserved-novus-pool" // unchanged for now
}
```
Jess (oncall): monitoring. querying logs: `kubectl logs -l app=gateway -c proxy --since=5m | grep novus | tail -n 200`
Amanda L: Novus SRE (via email) asks for ETA and whether this will require client changes. Sasha - can you message them?
Sasha S (SE): messaging now. telling them no client changes expected; we may ask them to keep clients on a short backoff just in case.
Murat K: canary logs look promising, error rate dropped ~70% for route novus in the last 90s. sample trace:
```
[2026-03-15T13:10:21Z] route=novus conn=abcd1234 event=ws_close code=1006 backend=10.0.8.45 latency_ms=1520
[2026-03-15T13:11:03Z] route=novus conn=abcd5678 event=proxy_error code=502 backend=10.0.8.46 latency_ms=18
[2026-03-15T13:12:10Z] route=novus conn=abcd9012 event=ws_open
```
Jess (oncall): good. continue canary for 10m, if error rate stays down, promote. also throttle incoming retries at gateway edge: set `retry_jitter` and short-circuit redundant retries from same conn. Murat, add a rate limit for per-conn retry attempts.
Murat K: applying per-conn retry limit + jitter change now. patch:
```
retry_policy {
  max_attempts_per_conn = 3
  jitter_ms = 250-1000
  short_circuit_on_rate = true
}
```
DeployBot: Config canary promoted to 30% for Novus route.
Jess (oncall): monitoring metrics dashboard: `ws_close_rate`, `backend_502_rate`, `per_conn_retry_count`. so far downward trend continues.
Amanda L: engineering leadership + account team looped in, prepping status update for Novus. Sasha will coordinate customer comms.
Sasha S (SE): update: Novus confirms sessions are stabilizing, decreased client retries manually enabled. They still observe occasional single-client flaps but overall throughput is back.
Devon R (next-oncall): I'll take the handoff at 13:40 UTC. leave any open action items for me?
Jess (oncall): action items: 1) keep canary for 20m 2) if stable, roll to full for Novus only (no global rollback). 3) run `wscat` check from our probe to simulate client ping/poang: `wscat -c wss://gw.example.com/novus -H 'x-tenant: novus' --ping=5000`
Murat K: noted. scheduling full promotion in 25m if metrics remain stable. I'll also add a temporary rule to route Novus to their reserved pool if we see any regression.
Amanda L: thanks team. tagging OpsPager to keep watches for the next hour. :eyes:
OpsPager: Watch acknowledged, 60m window. Escalation to infra team if `backend_502_rate` > 5% sustained for 5m.
Jess (oncall): handoff to Devon in 5. leaving runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gateway-ws-timeouts
Devon R (next-oncall): thanks, taking over. if anything spikes ping me directly.
Murat K: promoting full config for Novus route now after 18m of stable canary.
DeployBot: Promotion complete: gateway-config/2026-03-15/novus-ws-mitigation -> prod (route=novus).
Sasha S (SE): Novus confirms restoration from their side. great work.
Jess (oncall): closing P1 after 45m. final postmortem will include: why canary config interacted poorly with default client retry patterns, add tests for backoff/jitter on gateway, and add automated route-fallback to reserved pools for enterprise VPC tenants when streaming error rates spike.
Amanda L: filing incident ticket and assigning owners for follow-ups (runtime tests -> Murat, runbook updates -> Jess, customer comms docs -> Sasha).
Devon R (next-oncall): acknowledged.
IncidentBot: Incident P1 transitioned to RESOLVED by Jess at 2218887899.
